title: Breath rises, and all rise
hook: the powers of the body brag that they hold it up, and breath settles the argument by starting to walk out
carry: prana: the power all the others ride on
tomorrow: if breath is king, where does breath come from?

segments.voice: Yesterday: rayi and prana, matter and breath, and the two paths. Your line was the ancestors' path returns; the gods' path doesn't.
screen: `THE ANCESTORS' PATH RETURNS; THE GODS' PATH DOESN'T.`

segments.voice: A group project, the night before it's due. Who really carried this? The one who wrote it says the writing. The one who presented says the presentation. The one who booked the room says nobody would've had anywhere to meet. Then the quiet one who did the actual research gets up to leave, and suddenly everyone sees what they were standing on. Bhargava, from Vidarbha, the second student, asks Pippalada: how many gods hold up a living being? Which of them make it shine? Which is greatest? Pippalada answers with exactly that argument.
screen: `WHO REALLY CARRIED THIS?` → `THE QUIET ONE GETS UP TO LEAVE.` → `WHICH GOD IS GREATEST?`

segments.voice: The gods of the body, Pippalada says, are space, wind, fire, water and earth, and speech, mind, the eye and the ear. One day they shine with pride and declare: we hold up this body. We keep it standing. Then breath, prana, the chief of them all, says: don't be deluded. It's me. I divide myself five ways, and I hold it up. They don't believe him. So breath, out of pride, begins to rise, as if to leave. And as he rises, all the others are pulled up with him. When he settles back down, they all settle. The text gives a picture any village would know. When the king bee rises, all the bees rise. When it settles, they all settle. So it was with speech, mind, eye and ear. Then the gods, convinced, sing breath's praises. He burns as fire. He is the sun, the rain, the wind, the earth. He is what is and what isn't, and what never dies. Earlier this year, in the Chandogya, the senses took turns leaving. Here breath only has to begin to stand. The text sums it up with a wheel: as spokes are fixed in the hub, everything is fixed in breath. And the praise ends with a prayer: protect us as a mother protects her children. That's the teaching. Prana, the life-breath, is the power every other power rides on, and Hindus treat it as sacred. Some traditional families still offer the first small sips of a meal to the breaths, whispering pranaya svaha, before anyone eats.
screen: `SPEECH, MIND, EYE, EAR: WE HOLD IT UP.` · `BREATH: IT'S ME, DIVIDED FIVE WAYS.` · `BREATH RISES; ALL RISE WITH IT.` · `LIKE BEES WITH THEIR KING.` · then, large: `PRANA.`

segments.voice: Breathe normally, and at the top of an in-breath pause for a moment, nothing strained, and see whether everything seems to wait: the thoughts, the listening, the sense of the room. Then let the breath go on, and feel it all start moving again. After two or three, let breath carry the body without your help.
Prana, breath, the chief of the body's powers. Speech, mind, eye and ear all claim to hold the body, until prana begins to leave and they all rise with it.
Your line: prana, the power all the others ride on. Tomorrow, a student asks where breath itself comes from. Day four hundred seven, done.
